dimensions.note: Delta review for 2026.10.22.1 (hygiene cards #435/#436). Carried from the 2026.08.05.3 review; code for this dimension unchanged since (git log), and not re-reviewed in this delta. applicationKey is .meta({ sensitive: true }) and wired from a vault or an env reference; the 24h authorizationToken is a bearer credential that is never logged and never written into a resource. Notification rules add two secret surfaces — hmacSha256SigningSecret and arbitrary custom header values — and redactNotificationRule strips both before any snapshot.

Delta review for 2026.10.22.1 (hygiene cards #435/#436). Carried from the 2026.08.05.3 review; code for this dimension unchanged since (git log), and not re-reviewed in this delta. 64 tests, all mocked, plus a full live write cycle: create -> sync -> update -> delete against real B2, with the lifecycle rule round-tripping and the retention window moving 1 -> 2 days. A separate live run proved the visibility round trip allPrivate -> allPublic -> allPrivate and that a lifecycle-only update leaves visibility untouched. Fixes are proven by mutation in both directions — removing the public-bucket guard from update's execute leaves the bucket-visibility check passing its own test green while --input bucketType=allPublic sails through, which is exactly why the guard does not live only in the check.

Delta review for 2026.10.22.1 (hygiene cards #435/#436). Carried from the 2026.08.05.3 review; code for this dimension unchanged since (git log), and not re-reviewed in this delta. Two checks, both labelled policy and scoped to create/update so they genuinely auto-fire. The recorded issue is a platform boundary that operators must understand: swamp gives a check the model's global arguments but NEVER the method's inputs, so neither check can see --input. lifecycle-hidden-version-retention therefore fails a create that supplies rules via --input, and its error now says so explicitly rather than claiming nothing was declared. bucket-visibility would likewise be blind to --input bucketType=allPublic, so the authoritative guard for that lives inside create/update and the README states which layer is load-bearing. Verified live: the refusal fired, and the waiver was initially untypeable because `swamp model method run` has no --global-arg flag — allowPublicBucket is now a method input too.
